prompt.context_jp: 午後の応接室は、日差しが斜めに差し込んで静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 午後の応接室___、日差しが斜めに差し込んで静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the reception room as the scene being described?

feedback.correct_en: は sets 応接室 as the topic/stage whose state (quiet, sun streaming in) is being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the room as new information, but here it's the established setting whose atmosphere is being painted.

contrast_examples.en: The reception room was quiet. (describing the known setting)
A reception room came into view. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 午後の応接室は、日差しが斜めに差し込んで静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 午後の応接室は、日差し___斜めに差し込んで静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the sunlight as new descriptive information?

feedback.correct_en: が marks 日差し as new, observed information inside the subordinate clause describing the room.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly re-topicalize within the describing clause, breaking the scene-setting flow.

contrast_examples.en: The wind is cold. (commenting on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 電話越しに聞こえた唯の声は、いつもの気の強さを失って震えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 電話越しに聞こえた唯の声___、いつもの気の強さを失って震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Yui's voice as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 唯の声, then the sentence describes what was happening to it (trembling).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the voice as newly discovered, but the narrator is commenting on its quality.

contrast_examples.en: A voice could be heard. (new perception)

prompt.context_jp: 姪のモモが公園の遊具から落ちたと知り、メイは受話器を置くが早いか…
prompt.prompt_jp: 姪のモモ___公園の遊具から落ちたと知り、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Momo in this piece of news?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a と知り clause reporting new information, が marks Momo as the newly-reported subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly frame Momo as an already-established topic; this is news Mei just learned.

contrast_examples.jp: 息子が倒れたと聞いた。

prompt.context_jp: 妹の家の玄関に転がり込んだとき、廊下の奥から漂ってきたのは、意外にも穏やかな静けさだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 廊下の奥から漂ってきた___、意外にも穏やかな静けさだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this cleft identifying what was wafting in?

feedback.correct_en: のは…だった sets up a topical cleft: 'what wafted in was X'. The X slot is contrasted with expectations.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would require a different predicate pattern; here the narrator frames it as 'as for what wafted in, it was...'.

contrast_examples.en: What I saw was the sea.
(Marked, exhaustive focus on the event itself.)

prompt.context_jp: モモは幼い眉根を寄せて眠っており、その頬にはうっすらと絆創膏が貼られていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: モモ___幼い眉根を寄せて眠っており、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Momo as the topic of this descriptive sentence?

feedback.correct_en: Momo is already known; は topicalizes her so the sentence describes her state.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Momo as newly spotted, but she's the established focus of concern.

prompt.context_jp: だって 先に お姉ちゃんにかけたら つながらなかったし それに言おうと思ったら お姉ちゃん 最後まで話 聞かないで 切っちゃうし
prompt.prompt_jp: 先に お姉ちゃん___かけたら つながらなかったし
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'to older sister' as 'at least her, I called first'?

feedback.correct_en: かける (to call on the phone) takes に to mark the recipient of the call.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 姉 the direct object, which doesn't match 電話をかける pattern (the recipient is marked with に).

prompt.context_jp: 妹の家を辞したのは、日が傾き始めた頃だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妹の家を辞したのは、日___傾き始めた頃だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the sun in this scene-setting subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/time clause describing when, が marks 日 as the subject of the descriptive event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は cannot normally appear inside this kind of relative clause marking the subject.

prompt.context_jp: 扉の向こうに立っていたのは、息を切らせた鴫野ナギサだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 扉の向こうに立っていた___、息を切らせた鴫野ナギサだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this cleft revealing who was at the door?

feedback.correct_en: のは…だった is a topicalizing cleft: 'the one standing there was Nagisa'. The narration pivots to reveal identity.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが with だった sounds unnatural here; this pattern requires のは.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was a friend.
The problem was that he came. (nominalized event)

prompt.context_jp: 元栓が閉じられた瞬間、部屋を満たしていた水音が嘘のように途絶えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋を満たしていた水音___嘘のように途絶えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the water sound that stopped?

feedback.correct_en: が presents the sudden stopping as an observed event — neutral description of the main clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize the sound and sound more like commentary; the writer is narrating the instant event.

prompt.context_jp: 何で洗濯機の上に炊飯器が？
prompt.prompt_jp: 何で洗濯機の上___炊飯器が？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the location where the rice cooker exists?

feedback.correct_en: に marks the location of existence (a thing sitting somewhere).
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks where an action takes place, not where something exists.

contrast_examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: こんな生活 続けてたら 体 壊しますよ
prompt.prompt_jp: こんな生活___続けてたら 体 壊しますよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks '(this kind of) life' as the thing being continued?

feedback.correct_en: 続ける is transitive and takes を on its object (the lifestyle being continued).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark subject, but 生活 is what she's doing, not what's acting.

prompt.context_jp: 液晶に浮かんだのは、あの田所の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 液晶に浮かんだ___、あの田所の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits this identifying cleft?

feedback.correct_en: のは…だった topicalizes 'what appeared' and reveals its identity as Tadokoro's name.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが with だった does not form this reveal pattern; のは is standard for 'what appeared was X'.

contrast_examples.jp: 届いたのは手紙だった。

contrast_examples.en: It was yesterday that it arrived.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサさん 来月から 本社に異動になるみたいですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサさん 来月から 本社___異動になるみたいですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the destination of the transfer?

feedback.correct_en: 異動する/になる takes に to mark the destination you are moving to.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the place of activity, not the target of the transfer.

prompt.context_jp: 相原さん 最近 雰囲気が変わったわね
prompt.prompt_jp: 相原さん 最近 雰囲気___変わったわね
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the atmosphere/vibe that changed?

feedback.correct_en: が marks 雰囲気 as what has changed — a newly observed phenomenon about Aihara.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 雰囲気 as a known topic, but Higo is pointing out something newly noticed.

contrast_examples.en: Your hairstyle changed, didn't it. (new observation)
As for her hair, it's short. (describing a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサさんがいない生活なんて 考えられない
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサさん___いない生活なんて 考えられない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this relative clause 'a life without Nagisa-san'?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 生活, the subject takes が. は cannot normally appear there.
feedback.incorrect_en: は is restricted to main-clause topicalization; it doesn't fit inside this modifier.

prompt.context_jp: その視線には、雇い主が家政夫を評価する類の冷たさは微塵もなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その視線に___、…冷たさは微塵もなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'in that gaze' as the topic/location frame?

feedback.correct_en: には topicalizes the location-frame: 'as for in that gaze, there was no coldness'.
feedback.incorrect_en: にが is not grammatical; the に-marked location needs は to serve as the sentence topic.

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋には誰もいない。
contrast_examples.en: In this room, there's no one.
Someone is in this room. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 教育部門のマネージャーに なってほしいって
prompt.prompt_jp: 教育部門のマネージャーに ___ってほしいって
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits: 'they want you to become manager'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜になってほしい = 'want (someone) to become X'. The role is a new position he'd take on.
feedback.incorrect_en: やってほしい ('want you to do it') or いってほしい ('want you to go') don't fit the 'become manager' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: I want you to become a teacher.
I want you to do this.

prompt.context_jp: 他のスタッフに 引き継ぎをしないとですね
prompt.prompt_jp: 他のスタッフに ___をしないとですね
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun means 'handing over duties'?

feedback.correct_en: 引き継ぎ = handover of duties, the standard business term for transferring work to someone else.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き返し = turning back; 引き出し = drawer/withdrawal. Neither describes transferring work responsibilities.

prompt.context_jp: そこに白羽の矢が立ったのが、目の前の男だったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこに___の矢が立ったのが、目の前の男だったのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom meaning 'to be singled out / chosen'.

feedback.correct_en: 白羽の矢が立つ is the set idiom meaning 'to be the one chosen/singled out'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 黒羽 or 赤羽 are not part of any idiom here; only 白羽 completes this expression.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に白羽の矢が立った。

prompt.context_jp: 塵も積もれば山となるとはよく言ったもので、…
prompt.prompt_jp: ___も積もれば山となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb: 'Even X, piled up, becomes a mountain'.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる — 'even dust piled up becomes a mountain'. A classic proverb about small things adding up.
feedback.incorrect_en: The fixed form uses 塵 (dust/trash); 雪 or 水 are not part of this set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

contrast_examples.jp: 小さな努力が実を結ぶ。

prompt.context_jp: プロですから これぐらいの お部屋のほうが 片づけがいがあります
prompt.prompt_jp: これぐらいの お部屋のほうが 片づけ___があります
prompt.prompt_en: Which suffix forms 'worth the effort to tidy'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜がいがある ('worth doing') attaches to verb stems: 片づけがい = 'worth tidying'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜かた = 'way of doing' (manner), 〜ぶり = 'manner/after an interval'. Neither conveys 'worth doing'.

prompt.context_jp: 余裕なフリしてるけど いつも いっぱいいっぱいで
prompt.prompt_jp: いつも ___で
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'at my limit / overwhelmed'?

feedback.correct_en: いっぱいいっぱい means being at one's emotional/capacity limit — Mei admits she's always barely coping.
feedback.incorrect_en: ぎりぎり means 'just barely (in time)', ばらばら means 'scattered/in pieces'. Neither captures the feeling of being overwhelmed inside.

contrast_examples.jp: もういっぱいいっぱいだ。

prompt.context_jp: 何だか 少し… うん 肩の力が抜けた感じがする
prompt.prompt_jp: 肩の___が抜けた感じがする
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom meaning 'to relax / unwind'.

feedback.correct_en: 肩の力が抜ける literally 'strength leaves the shoulders' — the set phrase for relaxing after long tension.
feedback.incorrect_en: 肩の気 / 肩の手 are not fixed phrases; the expression uses 力 specifically.

contrast_examples.en: Relax your shoulders / take it easy.

prompt.context_jp: トライアルで 私と 結婚生活を 送りませんか？
prompt.prompt_jp: トライアルで 私と 結婚生活を ___ませんか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 結婚生活 (married life)?

feedback.correct_en: 生活を送る is the standard collocation — 'to lead/live a (married) life'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 過ごす collocates with 時間 or periods, and 歩む fits 人生 but not 生活 directly. 送る is the fixed match for 生活.

prompt.context_jp: Yui tells Nagisa about his transfer.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'you're being transferred to headquarters next month'?

choices.text: 来月から本社に異動になるみたいですよ
来月から本社で異動になるみたいですよ
来月から本社を異動になるみたいですよ

feedback.correct_en: 異動になる takes に for the destination of the transfer — this is the natural Japanese phrasing.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks where an action happens (not the target), and を doesn't work for destination of movement verbs like this.

prompt.context_jp: Higo advises Mei about someone who makes her feel lighter.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'you must never let go of someone like that'?

choices.text: そういう人は 絶対に手放しちゃダメよ
そういう人は 絶対に手を放しちゃダメよ
そういう人は 絶対に離れちゃダメよ

feedback.correct_en: 手放す ('to let go / give up') is one word used metaphorically for relationships — the natural idiomatic choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を放す literally means physically releasing a grip; 離れる means 'become distant' (intransitive, wrong subject).

contrast_examples.jp: 大切な人を手放さないで。
contrast_examples.en: Don't let go of someone precious.

prompt.context_jp: Nagisa warns Mei about her lifestyle.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'you'll ruin your health'?

choices.text: こんな生活 続けてたら 体 壊しますよ
こんな生活 続けてたら 体 割りますよ
こんな生活 続けてたら 体 傷みますよ

feedback.correct_en: 体を壊す is the standard collocation for ruining one's health through overwork or bad habits.
feedback.incorrect_en: 体を割る isn't a health idiom (it sounds physical/comedic), and 体が傷む is used for things like skin or food, not general health.

contrast_examples.jp: 無理すると体を壊すよ。
contrast_examples.en: If you push too hard, you'll wreck your health.

prompt.context_jp: Tadokoro desperately calls Nagisa for help.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally conveys 'it's got to be you — no one else will do'?

choices.text: ナギサさんじゃないと ダメなんです
ナギサさんじゃなくて ダメなんです
ナギサさんじゃなければ ダメなんです

feedback.correct_en: 〜じゃないとダメ is the natural colloquial pattern for 'it has to be X / nothing else will do'.
feedback.incorrect_en: じゃなくて is 'not X, (rather Y)' — wrong meaning. じゃなければダメ is grammatical but stiff/formal and less natural here.

contrast_examples.jp: これじゃないとダメだ。
contrast_examples.en: It has to be this one.

contrast_examples.jp: これじゃなくて、あれだ。

prompt.context_jp: Mei stumbles into a proposal.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally captures her hesitant proposal?

choices.text: じゃあ 私たち… 結婚しませんか？
じゃあ 私たち… 結婚しましょうか？
じゃあ 私たち… 結婚したいですか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜ませんか is the standard invitational form for proposing something — polite but personal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ましょうか sounds more like 'shall we (I'll decide)?' and 〜たいですか asks about the other's desire, awkward for a proposal.
